title: Rhetoric of Written Argument
description: Writing and reading as critical inquiry, designed to help students undertake university-level writing projects. Focus on rhetoric of written arguments. Students learn to use sources in their writing and make appropriate decisions about structure, cohesion, and rhetorical conventions.
notes: Not open to students with credit in a higher-numbered composition course or

title: Artificial Intelligence and Human Creativity
description: Exploration of the relationship between Artificial Intelligence and Human Creativity. To include analysis of historical representations of disembodied intelligences, close readings of digital interfaces and storage systems, and contemporary electronic literature.

title: Comics and History
description: Aesthetics, interplay of texts and images, visual communication, and changes over time.

title: Introduction to Horror Aesthetics
description: Criticism, history, and theory of horror aesthetics in horror comic books, film, literature, podcasts, radio, theatre, video games, and more.

title: Introduction to Children’s Literature Aesthetics
description: Introduction to aesthetics, criticism, history, and theory of children’s literature. Focus on children’s literature as an artistic, technical, and creative medium.

title: Rhetoric of Written Arguments in Context
description: Further practice in writing, reading, and critical thinking. Emphasis on rhetoric of written arguments in context and using multiple sources in writing. Continued attention to structure, cohesion, and rhetorical conventions.
notes: Not open to students with credit in AFRAS 200, AMIND 225, CCS 200, LING 200, or RWS 200. Completion of RWS 200 may require completion of the library workbook assignment.

title: The Art of Literature
description: Introduction to aesthetics, criticism, history, and theory of literature. Focus on literature as an artistic, creative, and technical medium.

title: Introduction to Children’s Literature
description: Introduction to the philosophical, critical, cultural, and political dimensions and implications of literature for children in different historical and cultural contexts. To include study of the issues, themes, and ideas that children’s texts engage.

title: Literature, the Self, and Society
description: Literary depictions of the self in society and the personal relevance of these depictions. Individual identity and psychology. Impacts of class, embodiment, gender, race, sexuality on selfhood, socialization.

title: Introduction to Literature of the United States
description: Introduction to key issues, methods, and texts in the study of Literature of the United States. Development of a broad and rigorous understanding of the concerns and debates that currently characterize the study of American literature.
notes: Not open to students with credit in ENGL 250A or ENGL 250B.

title: Introduction to British Literature
description: Introduction to key issues, methods, and texts in the study of British Literature. Development of a broad and rigorous understanding of the concerns and debates that currently characterize the study of British literature.
notes: Not open to students with credit in ENGL 260A or ENGL 260B.

title: Introduction to Comparative Literature
description: Introduction to key issues, methods, and texts in the field of Comparative Literature. Emphasis on comparative study of literature from diverse historical epochs and cultural traditions. May include the relation of literature to other arts.
notes: Not open to students with credit in C LT 270A or C LT 270B.

title: Introduction to Creative Writing
description: Reading, analysis, and practice of poetry and fiction. Includes analysis of works of poetry and fiction from a variety of critical perspectives to help students “read as writers” and to focus on how creative writing is developed.

title: Topics in Literature
description: Introduction to the study of specific topics in literature. Focus on a specific movement, theme, figure, genre, etc.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.

title: The Psychological Novel
description: Psychological novel from its inception to present, including major works from a variety of cultures. Readings designed to aid students in discovering insights which great novelists have unearthed in their explorations of the human psyche.

title: Literature and Environment
description: Environmental thought and consciousness as expressed in literature, emergence of modern and contemporary environmental thought, and impacts of literature on environmental awareness.

title: Children’s Literature and Advanced Composition
description: Critical and historical analysis of children’s literature in a variety of genres and forms.

title: Children’s Literature and Advanced Composition
description: Advanced composition; improvement of student skills through writing assignments based upon reading and work in the lecture part. Primarily designed to meet Graduation Writing Assessment and Literature requirements for Liberal Studies-Emphasis in Education.
notes: Satisfies the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement (GWAR) for students who get a minimum grade of C or Cr. Upper-division courses should only be taken by students who have completed 60 semester units or more. In exceptional cases, a student who has completed fewer than 60 units may enroll in upper division courses.

title: Literary Study: Analysis, Research, and Writing
description: Methods of literary analysis; concepts and terminology of literary study; research methods. Modes of writing about literature, with emphasis on the research paper.
notes: Satisfies the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement (GWAR) for students who get a minimum grade of C or Cr. Upper-division courses should only be taken by students who have completed 60 semester units or more. In exceptional cases, a student who has completed fewer than 60 units may enroll in upper division courses.

title: Chicana and Chicano Literature
description: Ideas, forms, history of significant Chicana and Chicano prose, poetry, and other literary genres.

title: African American Literature to 1900
description: Eighteenth and nineteenth century writing by African American authors. Issues of literary form, canon formation, and sociopolitical impact of the literature upon African American culture.

title: African American Literature After 1900
description: Writing by African American authors after 1900. Issues of literary form, canon formation and sociopolitical impact of the literature upon African American and American culture of the twentieth and twenty-first centuries.

title: Childhood’s Literature
description: Analysis of influential and/or neglected literature for children and young adults in a variety of genres and forms.
notes: Not applicable to English or comparative literature majors. Majors are to take

title: Science Fiction
description: How authors have responded to growing impact of science and technology on people’s lives and imaginations. Representative works by authors such as Kobo Abe, Bradbury, Butler, Delaney, DeLillo, Dick, Gibson, Heinlein, Hoban, Huxley, Kapek, LeGuin, Murakami, Orwell, Poe, Russ, Shelley, Verne, Wells, Zamyatin, and others.

title: African Literature
description: Comparative study of African literature as well as Black literature of North and South America and the Caribbean; intercontinental influences and the theme of Black identity.

title: LGBT Literature and Culture
description: LGBT knowledge and identities as expressed in literature and culture; changing nature of same-sex desire, sexual behavior, and same-sex relationships from antiquity to present.

title: Folk Literature
description: Studies in the ballad, bardic poetry, oral and popular literature and folklore.

title: Contemporary Topics in Literature
description: Exploration of writers, works and topics in fiction, poetry, drama, and film, emphasizing the relationship between literature and current concerns. Topics include the city in fiction and film, literature and identity, literature of death, literature of contemporary myth and folklore, women in literature. Primarily for the general student not specializing in English or comparative literature. May count only as an elective course toward the English major.

title: Literature and Film
description: Relationships between film and genres of literature, focusing on a critical comparison of the techniques of rhetoric, fiction, and drama and those of film. Topics include literature and film, novel into film, drama and film, reading film. Primarily for the general student not specializing in English or comparative literature. May count only as an elective course toward the English major.

title: Modern Fiction of the United States
description: Representative works by twentieth-century American authors such as Cather, Hemingway, Steinbeck, Faulkner, Fitzgerald, Ellison, Welty, Bellow, Vonnegut, Heller, Walker, others. Primarily for the general student not specializing in English or comparative literature. May count toward the English major only as an elective.

title: Internship
description: Practical work experience in a field related to English and comparative literature. Work performed under joint direction of activity sponsor and instructor.
notes: Not applicable to requirements for English and Comparative Literature majors.

title: Selected Topics in Literature
description: Specialized study of a selected topic in literature.

title: Seminar: English and Comparative Literature Honors Thesis
description: Capstone class to prepare students who have been accepted into the department’s honors program to write an undergraduate thesis by emphasizing advanced research methods and critical or creative writing skills.
notes: Not open to students with credit in ENGL 498.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.

title: Literature for Children
description: Critical, historical, and ideological analysis of literature intended for and read by children in a variety of genres and forms.
notes: This course cannot be used in place of

title: Adolescence in Literature
description: Critical, historical, and ideological analysis of adolescent literature to include works in a variety of forms and genres read by, written for, or that feature adolescents.

title: Topics in Children’s Literature
description: Topics in youth culture, literature, and media to include aesthetics, gender, multiculturalism, and sexuality. Fantasy, illustrated, non-fiction, and science fiction books.

title: The Writing of Criticism
description: Theory and practice of literary criticism. Emphasis on the work of important critics and on development of student’s own critical writing.
notes: Satisfies the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement (GWAR) for students who get a minimum grade of C or Cr. Upper-division courses should only be taken by students who have completed 60 semester units or more. In exceptional cases, a student who has completed fewer than 60 units may enroll in upper division courses.

title: Earlier Histories of British and American Literature
description: Historical movements and developments in English language literature before 1800.

title: Later Histories of British and American Literature
description: Historical movements and developments in English language literature after 1800.

title: Nineteenth Century European Literature
description: European literature of the nineteenth century or of a more limited period within that century.

title: Ethnic Literatures of the United States
description: Works from United States ethnic literatures, with emphasis on formerly excluded traditions as African-American, Hispanic and Chicano, Asian-American, and American Indian.

title: Literature of the United States, 1800-1860
description: Representative works by United States writers from 1800 to 1860; likely to include works by Emerson, Hawthorne, Melville, Poe, Stowe, Thoreau, Whitman, and others.

title: Literature of the United States, 1860-1920
description: Representative works by United States writers from 1860 to 1920; likely to include works by Charles Chesnutt, Kate Chopin, Stephen Crane, Emily Dickinson, Henry James, Mark Twain, Edith Wharton, and others.

title: Literature of the United States, 1920-1960
description: Representative works by United States writers from 1920 to 1960; likely to include works by Willa Cather, T. S. Eliot, William Faulkner, F. Scott Fitzgerald, Ernest Hemingway, Zora Neale Hurston, Eugene O’Neill, Katherine Anne Porter, Ezra Pound, John Steinbeck, and others.

title: Literature of the United States, 1960 to Present
description: United States writers from 1960 to the present; likely to include works by Edward Albee, Saul Bellow, Allen Ginsberg, Joseph Heller, Maxine Hong Kingston, Norman Mailer, Toni Morrison, Sylvia Plath, Adrienne Rich, Kurt Vonnegut, Eudora Welty, and others.

title: Topics in Literature of the United States
description: Topics in United States literature to include the literature of the South, Black writers in the U.S., the frontier and U.S. literature, the outcast in U.S. literature, the immigrant experience in U.S. literature.

title: Genre Studies
description: Study of a specific literary genre or genres, such as the novel, tragedy, epic, and lyric.

title: Authors
description: Works of a major author or, if useful comparisons and juxtapositions warrant, works of two or three authors, such as Jane Austen, Melville, Emerson, and Thoreau.

title: Chaucer
description: Chaucer’s works, with emphasis on The Canterbury Tales and Troilus and Criseyde.

title: Shakespeare
description: An introduction to the writings of Shakespeare.

title: Study of Shakespeare
description: Advanced study of Shakespeare’s achievement as poet and playwright.

title: British Literary Periods, Beginnings to 1660
description: Study of a literary period such as the Middle Ages or Renaissance.

title: Milton
description: Milton’s writings, with emphasis on Paradise Lost.

title: English Fiction
description: The development of English fiction from its beginnings to the end of the eighteenth century.

title: English Drama
description: English dramatic literature from its beginnings to the present. From the beginning to 1642.

title: English Drama
description: English dramatic literature from its beginnings to the present. Period following reopening of the theatres in 1660.

title: British Literary Periods, 1800-1900
description: Study of a literary period such as the Romantic or Victorian Age.

title: British Literary Periods, 1900-Present
description: Study of a literary period such as the Postmodern Era.

title: Queer Texts and Contexts
description: Queer knowledge and identities as expressed in literature and culture, to include queer theory, history, and experience.

title: Gothic Literary Tradition
description: Gothic literary tradition from its beginnings to the present day.

title: Literature in the Digital Age
description: Shifting literary landscape in the digital age. Adapting print-based literature and reading practices to a digital world and digital literary marketplace. Digital-born literature. New narrative and poetic forms for computational media.

title: Digital Methods in Literary Studies
description: Analyzing digitized literary texts and creating born-digital literature. Studying and creating literature digitally.

title: Literature and Culture
description: Study of literature in relation to a specific culture idea or phenomenon, such as literature and the law, literature and technology.

title: World Literatures
description: A comparative approach to themes and forms in world literatures (novel and short story). Focus of course to be set by instructor.

title: Ecocriticism
description: In-depth study of relationship between environment and literature to include ecocritical literary theory, history, and practice.
notes: Not open to students with credit in C LT 570.

title: Concepts in Comparative Studies
description: Basic concepts in comparative studies in literature (e.g., influence, movement, figure, genre, etc.); their validity, usefulness, and limitations.

title: Topics in Comparative Horror Studies
description: Comparative study of horror literature and other media to include film, music, television, and video games.

title: Chicanx Comix: Community, Storytelling, and Social Justice
description: A survey of noteworthy comic book titles by Americans of Mexican descent and other Latinx practitioners. Noteworthy works may include those of Lalo Alcaraz, Gilbert and Jaime Hernandez, Kayden Phoenix, and others. Topics include social justice movements, autobiography, and more.

title: Techniques of Poetry
description: Techniques of poetry from the writer’s point of view. Introduction to critical and theoretical literature on poetry. Includes a creative writing workshop.

title: Techniques of the Short Story
description: Techniques of the short story from the writer’s point of view. Introduction to critical and theoretical literature on the short story. Includes a creative writing workshop.

title: Techniques of the Novel
description: Techniques of the novel from the writer’s point of view. Introduction to critical and theoretical literature on the novel. Includes a creative writing workshop.

title: Poetry of Devotion: Hindu, Buddhist, Taoist and Sufi Voices
description: An exploration of Hindu, Buddhist, Taoist, and Sufi poetry; close readings of translated poetry, on topics such as longing, wisdom, insight, transcendence, and divine union; framing poets, poems, and poetic traditions within their historical and cultural context.

title: Literary Publishing and Editing Workshop A
description: Survey of literary publishing and editing industry. Practical experience in a variety of publishing and editing skills, interaction with industry professionals, and critical writing.

title: Literary Publishing and Editing Workshop B
description: Practical experience in small-press literary publishing. Creating and running a press to publish print and digital texts. Tutorials and guest lectures.

title: Techniques of Screenwriting
description: Techniques of screenwriting. Introduction to critical and theoretical literature on screenwriting. Includes a creative writing workshop.

title: Topics in Creative Writing
description: Techniques of creative writing focusing on a specialized genre such as comedy, science fiction, and biography. Study of the critical and theoretical literature on the genre. Includes a creative writing workshop.

title: Writing of Poetry
description: A creative writing workshop in poetry. Continuation of

title: Writing of Fiction
description: A creative writing workshop in fiction. Continuation of
notes: Satisfies the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement (GWAR) for students who get a minimum grade of C or Cr. Upper-division courses should only be taken by students who have completed 60 semester units or more. In exceptional cases, a student who has completed fewer than 60 units may enroll in upper division courses.

title: Writing Informal Essays
description: A creative writing workshop in nonfiction, especially the essay as an art form.
notes: Satisfies the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement (GWAR) for students who get a minimum grade of C or Cr. Upper-division courses should only be taken by students who have completed 60 semester units or more. In exceptional cases, a student who has completed fewer than 60 units may enroll in upper division courses.

title: Topics in Literature and the Arts
description: Comparative study of literature and other arts such as painting, sculpture, architecture, music, dance, and film.

title: Literature and Aesthetics
description: Theoretical and experiential investigation of relationships between literature and the other arts; literary works in context of an inquiry into aesthetics.

title: Selected Topics in Literature
description: Selected topics in literature.

title: Introduction to Graduate Study
description: Introduction to research methods and critical approaches common in the graduate study of literature and expository writing, with attention to basic reference works, bibliographical techniques, analytical strategies, scholarly frames of reference, and theory. Recommended for first-semester graduate students.

title: Seminar: Literary Period or Movement: American Literature
description: Advanced study, through its literature, of a literary period such as the Renaissance, or a movement such as American modernism.

title: Seminar: Literary Period or Movement: British Literature
description: Advanced study, through its literature, of a literary period such as the Renaissance, or a movement such as American modernism.

title: Seminar: Literary Period or Movement: Children’s Literature
description: Advanced study, through its literature, of a literary period such as the Renaissance, or a movement such as American modernism.

title: Seminar: A Literary Type: American Literature
description: Advanced study of a specific literary genre, such as the novel, tragic drama, lyric poetry, the personal essay, autobiography.

title: Seminar: A Literary Type: Children’s Literature
description: Advanced study of a specific literary genre, such as the novel, tragic drama, lyric poetry, the personal essay, autobiography.

title: British Literature
description: Selected works of an author, period, or subject in English literature.

title: Literature of the United States
description: Selected works of an author, period, or subject in literature of the United States.

title: Comparative Literature
description: Comparative approaches to literature: study of a theme, geographical region, external relationship, or of selected authors.

title: Form and Theory of Poetry
description: Poetry as a literary form.

title: Form and Theory of Fiction
description: Fiction as a literary form.

title: Special Topics
description: Intensive study in specific areas of English.

title: Seminar: A Major Author or Authors
description: Critical study of a major author or authors such as William Shakespeare, Charles Dickens, Edith Wharton, Marcel Proust, Gabriel García Márquez, Toni Morrison and others.

title: Seminar: Issues in British Literature
description: Advanced study of issues within the development of the novel in Great Britain, colonial literatures in English, the British lyrical tradition and others.

title: Seminar: Issues in Literature of the United States
description: Advanced study of such issues as postmodernity, regionalism, ethnicity, the urban experience, gender, the political novel.

title: Seminar: Issues in Comparative Literature
description: Advanced study of an issue such as translation, negritude, cultural studies, semiotics, deconstruction, or literature and censorship.
